details:
Implementation Plan

I've checked the code and am now writing the plan. Two findings shaped it:

- **Confirmed:** in `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, the `deterministic-skip-merge` job has no orchestrator integration-PR check at all.
- **Higher than reported:** `finalize_integration_merge_if_needed` (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10990`) treats `ai:ready-to-merge` on the tracking issue as permission to do the final merge. The skip job's linked-issue labelling could set that label, so the labels have to be blocked as well as auto-merge.

---

## Implementation plan: keep orchestrator integration PRs out of the deterministic-skip auto-merge path

**Planning ref:** checked-out ref `claude/zealous-rubin-bavor2`, HEAD `cb50a835b21af35fcfcf87425d62a05a05718576` (from the planning context). Integration branch metadata is `claude/zealous-rubin-bavor2`, and the mismatch flag is `false`.

### Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- This only changes existing code: one inline `run:` step in an existing job of `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`. No new script.
- Trigger: `review_autofix.yml`'s existing `deterministic-skip-merge` job (`needs: gate`, runs when `needs.gate.outputs.deterministic_skip == 'true'`). It runs on every PR event and dispatch that routes through `internal-review.yml` or the consumer `ai-review.yml`.
- No new long-running supervisor. No DB work. No `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends review_enable_auto_merge.sh integration-PR suppressor (ported inline into the deterministic-skip-merge job's existing head-ref suppressor chain)
Scope-mode justification: The finding names one gap: the deterministic-skip job enables squash auto-merge and applies merge-authorization labels without the integration-PR head-ref exclusion that `scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh` (lines 247–281) applies on the codex-agent path. The fix ports that exact match into the job's existing `PR_HEAD_REF` suppressor chain, next to the forward-merge fallback branch, reusing the gate's existing `head_ref` output (§14: no new API call).

The complete version (configured pattern, invalid-regex fallback to the canonical `^orchestrator/project-([0-9]+)$` match, and fail-closed on an empty head ref) costs well under 30 LOC more than a bare regex test, so it is included (Boil the Lake; §6 security > correctness).

Routing integration PRs away from the deterministic skip in the gate instead, so they always get a full reviewer run, is deliberately not done. It would add reviewer spend and change gate outputs that other jobs and tests rely on; the orchestrator's own readiness, security-pass and validation gates already own the final merge.

### 1. Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`
  - Job `deterministic-skip-merge` (around line 1879): add one `env:` entry, `ORCH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH_PATTERN: ${{ vars.ORCH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH_PATTERN || '^orchestrator/project-' }}`. This is the same expression already used at lines 513, 3856, 5693, 5723 and 5898.
  - Step `Mark PR review-skipped, mark linked issues ready-to-merge, enable auto-merge`: add the integration-PR exclusion (details in §2).
  - Gate `evaluate` step comment at around lines 1609–1614: it currently says an empty `head_ref` "never matches any suppressor regex, so auto-merge runs as before". Change it to say the deterministic-skip job now refuses merge authorization when `head_ref` is empty. Comment only, no logic change in the gate.
- `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py`: new contract test plus a behaviour test (see §6).
- `README.md`: in the `ENABLE_AUTO_MERGE` row, extend the "Orchestrator integration PRs … are unconditionally excluded" sentence to say this covers the deterministic-skip path too, which also skips the `ai:review-skipped` / `ai:ready-to-merge` labels.
- `changelog.d/6524-det-skip-integration-pr-exclusion.md`: new fragment under `<!-- changelog: fixed -->`, following CLAUDE.md §20 voice.
- Size check (§24): `review_autofix.yml` is 445,370 bytes on this ref. The change adds about 2–3 KB, which stays under the 480,000-byte guard. The implementer must re-check with `wc -c`. No script extraction is needed unless that check fails.

### 2. Functions / modules to implement
All of this goes inside the step's existing `run:` body.

**New helper** `deterministic_skip_head_ref_is_integration_pr` (name checked as unused in the workflow). It reads `PR_HEAD_REF` and `ORCH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH_PATTERN` and returns 0 when the head is an integration branch. It mirrors `review_enable_auto_merge.sh:247-262`:
- If the configured pattern is non-empty, test it with `printf '%s\n' "${PR_HEAD_REF}" | grep -Eq -- "${ORCH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH_PATTERN}"`.
- grep exit code above 1 (invalid ERE): emit `::warning::` and fall back to the canonical pattern.
- Empty pattern: emit `::warning::` and fall back.
- In every case, also match the canonical `[[ "${PR_HEAD_REF}" =~ ^orchestrator/project-([0-9]+)$ ]]`.

**New first branch** of the step-1 `if/elif` chain, placed before `if [ "${ENABLE_AUTO_MERGE}" != "true" ]`. Placing it first means labels are refused even when auto-merge is disabled.
- **Empty `PR_HEAD_REF`:** set `auto_merge_summary="REFUSED (gate-observed head ref unavailable)"`, log `AUTOFIX_DET_SKIP_MERGE_BOUND pr=${PR_NUMBER} head_sha=${PR_HEAD_SHA:-unknown} action=refuse reason=head_ref_unavailable` plus a `::warning::`, and leave `auto_merge_ready_labels_allowed="false"`.
- **Integration PR:** set `auto_merge_summary="SUPPRESSED (orchestrator integration PR head ref '${PR_HEAD_REF}'; orchestrator finalizes the merge)"`, log `AUTOFIX_DET_SKIP_MERGE_BOUND pr=… head_sha=… action=refuse reason=orchestrator_integration_pr`, and echo the canonical phrase `auto-merge suppressed on the deterministic-skip path` with a pointer to `finalize_integration_merge_if_needed`. Leave `auto_merge_ready_labels_allowed="false"`.
- In both cases the existing `if [ "${auto_merge_ready_labels_allowed}" != "true" ]` guard then writes the summary and exits 0. No `gh pr merge` runs, `ai:review-skipped` is not added, and no linked issue gets `ai:ready-to-merge`.
- The existing branches move to `elif` (ENABLE_AUTO_MERGE off, head-SHA check, forward-merge, squash) and are otherwise unchanged.

### 3. Data structures affected
- None persisted. Two new values of the local `auto_merge_summary` string, two new `reason=` values on the existing `AUTOFIX_DET_SKIP_MERGE_BOUND` audit line (the `action=refuse` value already exists), and one new job-level env var that reuses the existing repo variable name.

### 4. API / interface changes
- No new GitHub API calls. The head ref comes from the gate's existing `head_ref` output, which reuses its `/pulls/{n}` fetch (§14).
- Visible behaviour change, integration PRs only: a small or docs-only `orchestrator/project-*` PR on the deterministic-skip path no longer gets squash auto-merge, the `ai:review-skipped` label, or `ai:ready-to-merge` on its closing-reference issues. Gate outputs, job ids and step names are unchanged (§10).
- Empty gate `head_ref` now fails closed (refuse) instead of falling through to squash auto-merge. This only affects the anomalous case where the PR fetch returned no `head.ref`.

Failure modes:
- **Invalid `ORCH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH_PATTERN`** → `::warning::`, then canonical-pattern fallback, so `orchestrator/project-<n>` PRs are still excluded.
- **Empty head ref** → refuse plus warning. The PR stays open, and the next synchronize event or the orchestrator retries.
- **Integration PR** → nothing merges here. `finalize_integration_merge_if_needed` merges it after the security pass and validation.

## Decisions

### D1 — Exclude in the deterministic-skip job, not by suppressing the skip in the gate
- Chosen: add the head-ref exclusion to the `deterministic-skip-merge` step, before any merge enrolment or label write.
- Alternatives considered: (a) add an `INTEGRATION_SKIP_SUPPRESSED` flag in the gate so integration PRs always take the codex-agent path; (b) do both.
- Why: this matches the finding's recommendation, adds no reviewer spend or new gate-output semantics, and keeps the fix next to the existing forward-merge suppressor that already uses the same `PR_HEAD_REF` input. Integration PRs then rely on the orchestrator's own gates, which is the documented model in the README's `ENABLE_AUTO_MERGE` row.

### D2 — Refuse merge-authorization labels too, not just auto-merge
- Chosen: leave `auto_merge_ready_labels_allowed="false"` for integration PRs, so neither `ai:review-skipped` nor linked-issue `ai:ready-to-merge` is applied.
- Alternatives considered: copy the codex-agent helper exactly (`record_auto_merge_ready_labels_allowed "true"`), which suppresses auto-merge but still labels.
- Why: `finalize_integration_merge_if_needed` (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10990`) treats `ai:ready-to-merge` on the tracking issue as a final-merge gate (`tracking-ready-to-merge`). A doc-only integration PR whose body carried a closing keyword for the tracking issue (forbidden by §21 but possible in a hand-edited body) would let an unreviewed skip grant final-merge authorization. The issue explicitly asks for these labels to be excluded. The codex-agent helper is out of scope (Hold Scope); it is flagged under risks.

### D3 — Fail closed on an empty head ref
- Chosen: refuse merge authorization when `PR_HEAD_REF` is empty.
- Alternatives considered: keep the current fall-through to squash auto-merge.
- Why: an empty head ref means the integration check cannot be evaluated. `review_enable_auto_merge.sh:178` already fails closed in this case, and repo convention is fail-closed on ambiguous state.

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundary:** PR head ref and labels come from GitHub's authenticated `/pulls/{n}` response in the gate job, not from PR-controlled text. The head ref is author-chosen, but matching it can only *suppress* merging, never gr
